content: The test image shows multiple corn plants with extensive premature death — leaves are brown/tan and hanging limply, stalks standing but clearly dead. This points to a stalk rot or systemic wilt. Top candidates: Diplodia_stalk_rot, Anthracnose_stalk_rot, Charcoal_stalk_rot, Goss_wilt.

**Key observations from test image:**
- Mature corn plants with complete premature death — all leaves brown/tan, limp, hanging
- Stalks still standing upright (not lodged/fallen)
- Multiple adjacent plants affected
- No visible discrete leaf lesions — whole-plant death pattern

**Analysis:**
- Northern corn leaf blight, Goss_wilt, Stewarts_wilt, Physoderma — all show leaf-level lesion patterns on green tissue, not whole-plant death
- Charcoal/Diplodia/Anthracnose stalk rots all cause premature plant death but differ in internal stalk signs
- The **Anthracnose_stalk_rot** reference collage included a field-level panel (bottom right) showing nearly identical appearance: multiple plants with brown hanging leaves, standing stalks, premature death before lodging — this is classic "top dieback" progressed to full plant collapse
- Diplodia_stalk_rot reference showed only close-up stalk material; Charcoal_stalk_rot showed only internal stalk cross-sections
- The pattern of whole-plant death with upright stalks across multiple plants matches Anthracnose stalk rot's known progression from top dieback to full premature senescence
